subject: research/crn-twin
professional: a simulation-methodology statistician (discrete-event simulation, variance reduction; the Winter Simulation Conference / Management Science / ACM TOMACS audience) who has run common-random-numbers studies and written RNG stream-assignment code, plus a robotics evaluation engineer for the sim-ranking reading. They would check first that the correlation formula is right, that 'seed buys nothing' is not already the textbook synchronisation warning, and whether a model where policies differ only in draw count says anything about real controllers.

evidence.correctness: Ran the shipped code (PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests: 'Ran 8 tests in 2.08s OK'). Recomputed independently, sharing no code with the author: (a) exact rho with math.comb binomial pmfs and an explicit double sum; (b) a vectorised numpy simulation (1,000,000 episodes, cumsum of Bernoulli pointer shifts, take_along_axis) as a second route. All 16 profile x q cells of E1 agree: flat q=0.01/0.05/0.1/0.3 -> 0.9901/0.9523/0.9087/0.7666 (numpy MC 0.9901/0.9524/0.9088/0.7672; results.txt 0.990/0.952/0.909/0.767); discount 0.9944/0.9726/0.9463/0.8514 (results 0.994/0.973/0.946/0.851); ramp 0.9810/0.9100/0.8314/0.5987 (results 0.981/0.910/0.831/0.599); terminal 0.8179/0.3585/0.1216/0.0008 (results 0.818/0.358/0.122/0.001), and terminal equals (1-q)^20 as claimed. Independent sample-size arithmetic with statistics.NormalDist: independent streams n = 233.5 (README 233), terminal q=0.05 paired n = 149.79 (README 150). Independent numpy power simulation of the 'sizing trap' with a hard-coded t critical value 2.200985 (df 11), n=12, 40,000 reps: flat q=0.05 0.850 (E3 0.850), flat q=0.3 0.288 (0.285), terminal q=0.05 0.160 (0.156), terminal q=0.1 0.115 (0.111): all within Monte Carlo error. No wrong headline number found. One caveat, found by running: n_required uses normal quantiles, so 'flat q=0.01 needs 2.3 episodes' (whitepaper Result 2) is not attainable by the paper's own paired t-test: with n=3 its power is 0.745 (paired_test_power, 4000 reps) not 0.90. The 11 vs 12 flat q=0.05 figure agrees with the simulation only because df is large enough there.
evidence.completeness: Claims checked end to end: (1) closed-form rho and Var(R_A-R_B)=2 sigma_R^2 (1-rho): works, test + E1 + E2 + my recomputation; (2) terminal-only rho=(1-q)^T: tested to 12 places; (3) sizing trap powers 0.85/0.29/0.16/0.11 vs nominal 0.90: E3 present and I reproduced all four; (4) counter-keyed repair gives rho=1 exactly: tested, E4 present; (5) binary success ratios (0.263/0.459/0.718/1.006 stream, ~0.215 counter) in E5: present in results.txt, labelled simulation with no closed form, not independently re-run by me beyond the Gaussian machinery they share; (6) 'Live page' https://marisstella.app/research/crn-twin/: not loaded (offline audit); no research/crn-twin/project.json exists, so the card lives in the shared projects.json, not checked. Whitepaper, figure.py and SVG exist, no stubs or TODOs. Commands in the README ran as stated except experiments/run.py (~40 s), which I did not run in full: I recomputed its cells instead. Stated as not done and honestly so: noise-dependent replanning, signed weights, real simulator RNG, any robot data, combination with twin-evaluation. Everything the README claims is present; the claims are narrow.
evidence.verification: 8 unittest tests, run: all pass. Seven hand-seeded mutations, each reverted (diff against a backup after, and git status clean for the directory): M1 rho_exact truncation 't + d <= T' to '< T': FAILED (4 failures), caught. M3 pointer-shift probability 'rng.random() < q' to 'q / 2' in sample_pair: FAILED (2), caught. M5 counter mode no longer ignoring the offset (mode switch broken): FAILED (1), caught. M2 n_required one-sided quantile (1 - alpha instead of 1 - alpha/2): 8/8 OK, NOT caught. M4 paired_test_power critical value using alpha instead of alpha/2 (a one-sided test reported as two-sided, inflating power): 8/8 OK, NOT caught. M6 sample variance divisor n-1 to n inside paired_test_power: 8/8 OK, NOT caught. M7 ramp weights float(t+1) to float(t) (first weight becomes 0): 8/8 OK, NOT caught, because the ramp test compares the formula with a simulation using the same weights, which cannot see a wrong weight definition. So the rho formula and the shift model are well guarded, but n_required has only a ratio test (insensitive to the quantile), paired_test_power has no test at all although the sizing-trap headline (E3, the paper's Result 3) rests on it, and the discount/ramp profile definitions are unpinned. The test of the simulation uses 0.012 tolerance against 40,000 reps, adequate. Score 2: the core identity is protected, but 4 of 7 seeded bugs, three of them in the code behind a headline result, passed.
evidence.craft: Read src/crn_twin/model.py (~130 lines), tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py and the paper. Compact, pure-Python, readable, seeded, explicit __all__, docstring defining the model; rho_exact is an O(T^3) pmf walk that is fine at T=20; hand-rolled erf-bisection normal quantile and closed-form t CDF are accurate (t_quantile(0.975,10)=2.2281 tested). Concrete defects: (1) paired_test_power treats a zero sample standard deviation as a rejection ('if sd == 0.0 or ...: hit += 1'), so under the null (gap=0) in counter mode, where both returns are identical, it reports rejection rate 1.0 (I ran gap=0, n=5, counter: 1.0). The E4 'power 1.000' for the repair is that branch (the difference is constant), which is true for a positive gap but makes the function unusable as a size/type-I check and hides a degenerate case rather than flagging it; (2) no input validation: rho_exact(w, q=1.5) silently returns 60.2 (a 'correlation' of 60), q outside [0,1] and empty weights are not rejected; (3) n_required and the text 'n needed 2.3' use normal quantiles for a method (paired t-test) whose small-n power is lower, with no warning; (4) from .model import * in __init__; (5) E5's two loops reuse seeds 51/52 per mode so stream and counter columns share noise, which is fine but undocumented. No copied engine. Score 2: clean and small, but with a silent degenerate-branch bug and no validation.
evidence.claims: Checked claims and their backing: rho formula, 'matched to 30,000-episode simulation within 0.012' (E1 max difference 0.006 at terminal q=0.05; I confirmed with 1M draws); 'q = 0.05/0.3 gives rho 0.952/0.767' (E1 and my recomputation); 'terminal-only rho=(1-q)^T = 0.358/0.001' (tested, recomputed); 'episodes for 90%-power test: 233 independent, 11/55 flat, 150/233 terminal' (E2, recomputed; 11/55 are normal-approximation numbers, the t-test needs 12/55); 'power 0.85/0.29/0.11-0.16 against nominal 0.90' (E3, reproduced independently); 'counter-keyed draws restore rho=1 exactly' (test + E4). Limitations are frank: stylised Gaussian noise, policies differ only in draw count, events independent of noise, no robot data, the repair 'exactly zero' being an artefact of the model (the README says so). Attribution is correct and conservative: CRN is credited as classical (Law & Kelton 2000; Glasserman & Yao 1992; Salmon et al. 2011) and the university groups are named only as context with a no-affiliation statement, as the repo rule requires. Weaknesses: the claim 'a fixed seed buys nothing at q=0.3' is true for terminal-only scores only, and the sentence runs together with flat; 'whitepaper n needed 2.3' is not achievable (power 0.745 at n=3); the 'Builds on' sentence links the study to HIRO/ARPG/RECUV although nothing in it uses their work. The README is one dense paragraph. Disclaimer: this is research, not a product, so no usage tracking required.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can use this as a small, correct reference for one concrete phenomenon (a CRN seed pairs policies only as long as RNG read pointers stay aligned) and can copy rho_exact to size a paired comparison; the 'key each draw by (episode, step)' repair is immediately actionable. They cannot take a result to a venue. Nearest prior work: synchronisation of random-number use is the defining requirement of CRN in the simulation literature: Schruben & Margolin (1978, JASA) introduced assignment of dedicated streams per random source to keep CRN synchronised; Law & Kelton ch. 11 and Glasserman & Yao (1992) discuss loss of synchronisation and the standard cure (one stream or substream per source, per replication); L'Ecuyer, Simard, Chen & Kelton (2002, Oper. Res.) RngStreams provide exactly the stream/substream machinery that keys draws by (replication, source); Salmon et al. (2011) counter-based generators do it with a key. So the repair is textbook and the paper says so. What is new and sound: a closed-form correlation for the specific shifted-pointer model (Binomial(t,q) offset, weights w_t), the terminal-score (1-q)^T collapse, and the quantified power loss when n is planned on rho=0.95. That is a correct, small, citable calculation; it is not a research result at the bar of research/CLAUDE.md (a PhD-level programme aimed at a named venue), and the model (policies differ only in draw count, independent of noise) omits what actually decorrelates real controllers, state divergence, which the paper lists under limitations. No real simulator RNG was measured. Score 2: sound and useful as an application note, not buildable-upon as research.
evidence.domain: A simulation-variance-reduction statistician would accept the model's algebra and the conclusion, and note that it is the standard synchronisation point of Schruben-Margolin and Law-Kelton quantified for one tractable case. They would approve of paired t-test validity being kept (the failure is lost power, not a false alarm) and of reporting the binary-outcome case where pairing helps less. They would ask: why not measure rho on a real simulator (MuJoCo/PyBullet seeding) with two real controllers, since divergence in state, not pointer drift, is the practical cause; why the sizing uses normal quantiles at n near 2-3; why the null-size of the test is never examined (the zero-sd branch makes it 1.0 in counter mode); and why signed weights (e.g. difference-of-objectives, or penalty terms) are excluded, since they give rho below 0. Departures from practice are small and disclosed. Score 3.

defects.what: paired_test_power counts a zero sample standard deviation as a rejection. In counter mode with gap=0 (identical returns) the empirical rejection rate is 1.0 (ran n=5, 500 reps), so the function cannot check a test's size, and the E4 'power 1.000' headline comes from this branch.

Four of seven seeded mutations survived all 8 tests: n_required one-sided quantile, paired_test_power critical value, its variance divisor, and ramp weight definition. paired_test_power, behind the sizing-trap headline (E3, Result 3), has no test.
defects.where: research/crn-twin/tests/test_model.py (no test of paired_test_power, n_required absolute value, or weights('ramp'/'discount') values)

defects.what: Novelty is modest: the shared-seed synchronisation requirement and the per-source stream/substream repair are textbook CRN (Schruben-Margolin 1978; Law-Kelton; L'Ecuyer et al. 2002). The new content is a closed-form rho for one stylised shift model. Not at the PhD-programme bar of research/CLAUDE.md; no real simulator or robot data.
'n needed 2.3' episodes (flat, q=0.01) uses normal quantiles; the paper's own paired t-test at n=3 has power 0.745 against the nominal 0.90. Small-n entries should use the t quantile.
No input validation: rho_exact(w, q=1.5) returns 60.2 instead of raising; q outside [0,1] and empty weights are accepted.

verdict: A small, correct, honest piece of work. I recomputed the headline correlations two independent ways (an explicit binomial double sum and a 1M-episode vectorised numpy simulation) for all 16 profile-by-q cells, the 233 and 150 episode counts, and the four 'sizing trap' power figures with an independently coded t-test: everything matched the author's numbers to Monte Carlo error, and no headline number was wrong. It is finished as scoped and its limitations are stated frankly. It misses the bar on verification: seeded bugs in the correlation and shift logic were caught, but four of seven, including one that turns the power test one-sided and one in the ramp weight definition, passed, and the function behind the sizing-trap result has no test. The code also has a silent degenerate branch (zero standard deviation counted as rejection, null rejection rate 1.0 in counter mode). Against prior work the result is sound but mostly classical: the need to keep random streams synchronised, and the per-source stream fix, are the definition of CRN practice (Schruben & Margolin 1978; Law & Kelton; Glasserman & Yao 1992; L'Ecuyer et al. 2002); the closed-form correlation for a binomial pointer-shift model and the planning-power table are the new, citable parts. Not PhD-programme level. Meets the bar: no (verification 2). Finished: yes.
